summary: Matadi, capital of Kongo-Central province and the DRC's main seaport, lies far from the eastern conflict zones and no armed group holds territory in the city. Day-to-day order across its communes (Matadi, Mvuzi, Nzanza) and health-area neighbourhoods is kept by the Congolese National Police (PNC), with FARDC, naval and port-security elements also present. Security problems are urban crime (kuluna-type banditry) and periodic political unrest linked historically to the Bundu dia Kongo movement (notably 2017-2020), neither of which amounts to territorial control. The small 'Militaire' health area (Camp Redjaf military camp) is assessed as FARDC-run. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked), so the assessment rests on default state presence.

zones.description: Matadi city: all civilian health-area neighbourhoods (Soyo Luadi, Makindu, Hygiène, Salongo, Ngadi, Mvuzi, Banana, Ville Basse, Nzanza, Trabeka, Nzinga Lutete, Kitomesa, Baobab, Lieutenant Mpaka, Mbuzi Mongo) and the city as a whole
zones.evidence: Provincial capital and port in a province with no active armed-group territorial control; the PNC runs commissariats and handles arrests and order, with FARDC garrisoned in the city. Crime (kuluna) and past Bundu dia Kongo unrest (2017-2020) did not displace state control. No sources could be retrieved in this run.
Health area named 'Militaire' with alt name Redjaf corresponds to the FARDC Camp Redjaf; order inside a military camp is kept by the army (military police). No sources could be retrieved in this run.
